ev.rus_h_pantheon.title: Idols on the Hill
ev.rus_h_pantheon.text: Prince Vladimir has set up idols on the hill beyond his hall: Perun with a silver head and a golden moustache, Khors, Dazhbog, Stribog, Simargl and Mokosh. People bring them offerings.
ev.rus_h_pantheon.note: According to the Primary Chronicle, in 980 Vladimir Svyatoslavich, newly master of Kiev, set up idols of the pagan gods on a hill. Eight years later he was baptised and had them thrown down.
ev.rus_h_baptism.title: The Baptism
ev.rus_h_baptism.text: The prince has proclaimed: "Whoever does not come to the river tomorrow, rich or poor, beggar or slave, will be my enemy." Perun's idol is dragged to the Dnieper and beaten with sticks, and in the morning all Kiev wades into the water while Greek priests read prayers from the bank.
ev.rus_h_baptism.river: Wade into the Dnieper with everyone
ev.rus_h_baptism.forest: Slip off into the forest and wait
ev.rus_h_baptism.forest.success: You came back a week later. You will honour the old gods in secret.
ev.rus_h_baptism.forest.failure: Your neighbours noticed you were missing. You had to be baptised late, amid jeers.
ev.rus_h_baptism.note: The Baptism of Rus was Prince Vladimir Svyatoslavich's acceptance of Christianity around 988 and the mass baptism of Kievans in the Dnieper. The faith came from Byzantium with Greek clergy and the prince's marriage to the Byzantine princess Anna.
ev.rus_h_tithe_church.title: The Church of the Tithe
ev.rus_h_tithe_church.text: Greek masters have finished Kiev's first stone church, dedicated to the Mother of God. The prince has given it a tenth of his revenues. Inside are marble, mosaics and light falling from windows under the dome: nobody here has ever seen anything like it.
ev.rus_h_tithe_church.note: The Church of the Dormition, nicknamed the Church of the Tithe, was built in 989–996. In 1240, when the Mongols took Kiev, it collapsed under the weight of the people who had sought refuge on it.
ev.rus_h_boris_gleb.title: The War of Vladimir's Sons
ev.rus_h_boris_gleb.text: Prince Vladimir is dead, and Svyatopolk, who took Kiev, sent assassins after his brothers Boris and Gleb. Yaroslav has raised the Novgorodians and Varangians against him. War is spreading across the land.
ev.rus_h_boris_gleb.yaroslav.success: Yaroslav won. Svyatopolk was dubbed the Accursed, and Boris and Gleb were hailed as saints.
ev.rus_h_boris_gleb.yaroslav.failure: You were badly wounded in the fighting.
ev.rus_h_boris_gleb.aside: Wait while the princes fight over the land
ev.rus_h_boris_gleb.note: After Vladimir's death in 1015 his sons Boris and Gleb were murdered, and the blame fell on Svyatopolk. Yaroslav and his Novgorodians defeated him at Lyubech in 1016 and finally on the Alta in 1019. Boris and Gleb became the first saints of Rus.
ev.rus_h_pravda.title: Yaroslav's Law
ev.rus_h_pravda.text: Prince Yaroslav has given the Novgorodians a charter, a Law: how much to pay for a killing, a knocked-out tooth, a stolen horse. Blood vengeance is allowed only to close kin; otherwise it is a fine in silver.
ev.rus_h_pravda.note: The oldest part of the Russkaya Pravda, "Yaroslav's Law", was by chronicle tradition granted to the Novgorodians around 1016. It was later expanded by Yaroslav's sons (around 1072) and by Vladimir Monomakh.
ev.rus_h_sophia.title: Holy Wisdom
ev.rus_h_sophia.text: They are building the Cathedral of Holy Wisdom: Greek architects, local masons, hundreds of hod carriers. The walls of flat brick and stone are rising towards many domes. There is work for anyone not afraid of heights.
ev.rus_h_sophia.work: Hire on at the building site
ev.rus_h_sophia.watch: Come to watch on feast days
ev.rus_h_sophia.note: St Sophia in Kiev was built under Yaroslav the Wise from 1037 (some date it from 1011); St Sophia in Novgorod was built in 1045–1050 under his son Vladimir.
ev.rus_h_1068.title: The Assembly in the Market
ev.rus_h_1068.text: The Polovtsians have routed the princes on the Alta and spread across the land. The Kievans gathered in the market square: "Give us arms and horses, prince, and we will fight again!" Prince Izyaslav refused. The crowd is heading for the dungeon to free Prince Vseslav of Polotsk.
ev.rus_h_1068.join.success: Vseslav was carried out of the dungeon and proclaimed prince. In the chaos the prince's court was looted, and something came your way too.
ev.rus_h_1068.join.failure: The retainers charged the crowd. You took a beating.
ev.rus_h_1068.home: Bar the gate and stay home
ev.rus_h_1068.note: In 1068, after a defeat by the Polovtsians on the Alta, the Kievans rose, drove out Izyaslav Yaroslavich and enthroned Prince Vseslav of Polotsk, who had been held in a dungeon. Seven months later Izyaslav returned with a Polish army.
ev.rus_h_lyubech.title: The Congress at Lyubech
ev.rus_h_lyubech.text: The princes met at Lyubech, kissed the cross and said: "Why do we ruin the land of Rus, stirring up feuds among ourselves? Let each hold his own patrimony." Everyone breathed a sigh of hope, though not for long.
ev.rus_h_lyubech.note: The Congress of Lyubech in 1097 confirmed each prince in his patrimony. Almost immediately afterwards Prince Vasilko of Terebovl was blinded, and the feuds resumed.
ev.rus_h_salnitsa.title: Into the Steppe
ev.rus_h_salnitsa.text: Vladimir Monomakh has persuaded the princes to strike the Polovtsians not in summer but in early spring, while their horses are thin after the winter. Even peasants are being called up: "You pity the peasant and his horse, but not that a Polovtsian will carry off the peasant and all his household?"
ev.rus_h_salnitsa.march.success: At the Salnitsa the Polovtsians were broken. You came back with plunder: horses, weapons, carpets.
ev.rus_h_salnitsa.march.failure: A steppe arrow found you in the very first skirmish.
ev.rus_h_salnitsa.note: The campaigns of the Rus princes led by Vladimir Monomakh in 1103, 1107 and 1111 (the battle on the Salnitsa) drove the Polovtsians away from Rus for many years.
ev.rus_h_1113.title: The Rising Against the Usurers
ev.rus_h_1113.text: Prince Svyatopolk has died, under whom moneylenders charged merciless interest. The Kievans are sacking the house of the city captain and the moneylenders' homes, and looting the Jewish quarter too. The boyars have sent for Vladimir Monomakh.
ev.rus_h_1113.protect: Hide your neighbours in your house
ev.rus_h_1113.protect.success: You hid your neighbours in the cellar, and the mob went past.
ev.rus_h_1113.protect.failure: The mob burst into the yard. Your neighbours escaped, but you were beaten.
ev.rus_h_1113.note: The Kiev uprising of 1113 broke out after the death of Svyatopolk Izyaslavich. Vladimir Monomakh, invited to the throne, issued a "Statute on Interest" limiting rates on loans.
ev.rus_h_1136.title: The Prince Expelled
ev.rus_h_1136.text: The veche locked Prince Vsevolod and his household under guard in the bishop's court, then drove him from the city: "He does not look after the common folk, he wanted to rule in Pereyaslavl, he fled the battlefield." From now on Novgorod chooses its own princes.
ev.rus_h_1136.note: The expulsion of Prince Vsevolod Mstislavich in 1136 is traditionally seen as the start of the Novgorod Republic: from then on the prince ruled under a compact with the veche.
ev.rus_h_kiev_1169.title: Kiev Taken by Its Own
ev.rus_h_kiev_1169.text: The army of Andrei Bogolyubsky and his allied princes has taken Kiev by storm. For two days they loot the Podil, the Hill and the churches, carrying off icons, books, vestments and bells. Rus is plundering Rus.
ev.rus_h_kiev_1169.hide: Bury your valuables and lie low
ev.rus_h_kiev_1169.hide.success: The invaders never found your cache. You lost little.
ev.rus_h_kiev_1169.hide.failure: A neighbour gave the cache away. They took everything and beat you besides.
ev.rus_h_kiev_1169.church.success: For some reason that church was spared.
ev.rus_h_kiev_1169.church.failure: They looted the churches too. You were shoved out, the cross torn from your neck.
ev.rus_h_kiev_1169.note: In March 1169 an army sent by Prince Andrei Bogolyubsky of Vladimir-Suzdal took and plundered Kiev. Andrei himself stayed in Vladimir: seniority in Rus shifted to the north-east.
ev.rus_h_znamenie.title: The Sign
ev.rus_h_znamenie.text: The Suzdalian army laid siege to Novgorod. The archbishop carried an icon of the Mother of God onto the wall, an arrow struck it, and they say the icon turned its face to the city and wept. The Suzdalians were driven back; prisoners went so cheap, two nogatas a head, that the whole market laughed.
ev.rus_h_znamenie.note: On 25 February 1170 the Novgorodians repelled Andrei Bogolyubsky's army. The victory was credited to the wonder-working icon of the Sign; the chronicle says Suzdalian captives sold for 2 nogatas each.
ev.rus_h_bogolyubsky.title: Murder at Bogolyubovo
ev.rus_h_bogolyubsky.text: In the night boyars and servants murdered Grand Prince Andrei in his castle at Bogolyubovo. His body lay in the garden for two days while townsfolk and villagers plundered the prince's court, gold, cloth and vessels.
ev.rus_h_bogolyubsky.loot: Go along: it will all go anyway
ev.rus_h_bogolyubsky.note: Andrei Bogolyubsky was murdered by conspirators on the night of 29 June 1174. His death set off looting and civil war in the Vladimir land, ending with the accession of his brother Vsevolod Big Nest.
ev.rus_h_igor.title: Igor's Campaign
ev.rus_h_igor.text: Prince Igor of Novgorod-Seversky went against the Polovtsians without leave and was destroyed with his whole army in the steppe, taken captive himself. Now the Polovtsians are riding into Rus on his tracks, burning villages near Pereyaslavl.
ev.rus_h_igor.note: Igor Svyatoslavich's failed campaign of 1185 is described in the chronicles and became the subject of the "Lay of Igor's Campaign". Igor himself later escaped from captivity.
ev.rus_h_kalka.title: The Battle on the Kalka
ev.rus_h_kalka.text: An unknown people has appeared: "no one knows who they are or where they came from, what their tongue is or what tribe." The Polovtsians asked for help, the princes rode into the steppe, and on the river Kalka almost the whole army perished. The enemy vanished as suddenly as it had come.
ev.rus_h_kalka.note: On 31 May 1223, on the river Kalka, a Mongol force under Jebe and Subutai crushed the combined army of the Rus princes and the Polovtsians. Many princes died, among them Mstislav Romanovich of Kiev.
ev.rus_h_famine_1230.title: The Great Famine
ev.rus_h_famine_1230.text: An early frost killed the grain, and for a second year Novgorod is starving. People eat moss, bark, lime leaves. The poor sell themselves as slaves to foreign merchants. The dead are buried in common pits.
ev.rus_h_famine_1230.keep: Keep the stores for your own
ev.rus_h_famine_1230.note: The chronicle describes the famine of 1230–31 in Novgorod as a terrible disaster: thousands of dead were buried in common pits. German merchants who brought grain from overseas eased the crisis.
ev.rus_h_batu_vladimir.title: Batu's Host
ev.rus_h_batu_vladimir.text: In winter Khan Batu's enormous horde came along the frozen rivers. Ryazan has fallen, Moscow and Kolomna are burned. Now siege engines are battering the walls of Vladimir. Prince Yury has gone north to gather an army.
ev.rus_h_batu_vladimir.forest.success: You sat out the invasion deep in the forest. You came back to ashes.
ev.rus_h_batu_vladimir.forest.failure: A mounted patrol caught up with the refugees. You survived by a miracle.
ev.rus_h_batu_vladimir.walls.success: The city fell, but you broke out through a breach and got away.
ev.rus_h_batu_vladimir.walls.failure: They broke through the wall. You fell in the fighting at the Golden Gate.
ev.rus_h_batu_vladimir.note: In the winter of 1237–38 Batu's Mongol army devastated north-eastern Rus. Vladimir fell on 7 February 1238, and Grand Prince Yury Vsevolodovich died in battle on the river Sit on 4 March.
ev.rus_h_batu_kiev.title: The Fall of Kiev
ev.rus_h_batu_kiev.text: "You could not hear a human voice for the creak of carts, the bellowing of camels and the neighing of horses." Batu stands before Kiev, rams pounding at the Lyadsky Gate. People are running to the Church of the Tithe and climbing onto its vaults.
ev.rus_h_batu_kiev.flee: Flee across the Dnieper while you can
ev.rus_h_batu_kiev.flee.success: You escaped across the ice on the last night. Behind you a red glow rose over the Hill.
ev.rus_h_batu_kiev.flee.failure: They caught you on the ice. A rope, a wagon train, the road to the Horde.
ev.rus_h_batu_kiev.tithe: Take refuge in the Church of the Tithe
ev.rus_h_batu_kiev.tithe.success: The vaults collapsed beside you. You crawled out of the rubble at night.
ev.rus_h_batu_kiev.tithe.failure: The vaults could not bear the weight of so many people.
ev.rus_h_batu_kiev.note: Kiev was taken by Batu's army on 6 December 1240 (some sources say 19 November). The Church of the Tithe collapsed under the weight of those sheltering on it. Six years later the papal envoy Plano Carpini counted barely two hundred houses in the city.
ev.rus_h_neva.title: The Battle of the Neva
ev.rus_h_neva.text: The Swedes landed at the mouth of the Izhora. Young Prince Alexander, without waiting for reinforcements, fell on their camp and routed them. Novgorod rings every bell and calls the prince "of the Neva".
ev.rus_h_neva.note: On 15 July 1240 Prince Alexander Yaroslavich defeated a Swedish force on the Neva. The name "Nevsky" became attached to him later.
ev.rus_h_ice.title: The Battle on the Ice
ev.rus_h_ice.text: German knights have taken Pskov and are nearing the lands of Novgorod. Prince Alexander is raising a militia and leading it to Lake Peipus.
ev.rus_h_ice.go.success: On the lake ice the knights' wedge bogged down in the infantry and broke. You came home victorious.
ev.rus_h_ice.go.failure: You were wounded in the fighting on the ice.
ev.rus_h_ice.note: On 5 April 1242 Alexander Nevsky's army defeated a force of the Livonian Order and its allies on the ice of Lake Peipus.
ev.rus_h_census.title: The Census
ev.rus_h_census.text: The Horde's census takers have arrived to count people for tribute. Every household, every soul will be written in their scroll. People grumble and shout: "Let us die honourably for Holy Wisdom!"
ev.rus_h_census.resist: Shout against the census at the veche
ev.rus_h_census.resist.success: There was a long uproar but no bloodshed. The census takers counted the city another time.
ev.rus_h_census.resist.failure: Prince Alexander dealt with the troublemakers himself, cutting off noses and putting out eyes.
ev.rus_h_census.note: The Mongol censuses in Rus took place in 1257–59. Novgorod resisted the count for a long time, and Alexander Nevsky put down the unrest by force.
ev.rus_h_dudenev.title: Dyuden's Raid
ev.rus_h_dudenev.text: Prince Andrei of Gorodets, fighting his brother for the grand princely throne, brought the Horde army of Prince Dyuden. The Tatars took fourteen towns, among them Vladimir, Suzdal, Moscow and Pereyaslavl. Your house has been plundered.
ev.rus_h_dudenev.note: In 1293 the Horde commander Dyuden, called in by Andrei Alexandrovich, ravaged 14 towns of north-eastern Rus. It was one of the most devastating invasions since Batu.
ev.rus_h_kalita.title: The Great Calm
ev.rus_h_kalita.text: Prince Ivan Danilovich, nicknamed Kalita, "money bag", for his alms to the poor, has received the khan's patent for the grand princely throne and collects the Horde's tribute himself. Tatar collectors no longer ride from house to house. The chronicler writes: "a great calm descended."
ev.rus_h_kalita.note: Ivan Kalita received the khan's patent in 1328 (some say 1332). In his reign the metropolitan moved to Moscow, and Horde raids on north-eastern Rus stopped for a long time.
ev.rus_h_black_death.title: The Black Death
ev.rus_h_black_death.text: The plague has come from Pskov: a man begins coughing blood and is dead on the third day. They bury ten, twenty to a grave. In a single day the people put up a votive wooden church to pray for mercy.
ev.rus_h_black_death.care.success: The plague passed you by. People will not forget what you did.
ev.rus_h_black_death.care.failure: You came down with the fever.
ev.rus_h_black_death.isolate.success: You waited out the plague within your four walls.
ev.rus_h_black_death.isolate.failure: The sickness got into the house anyway.
ev.rus_h_black_death.church.success: The church went up in a day. Your heart felt lighter.
ev.rus_h_black_death.church.failure: Prayer did not protect you: you fell ill.
ev.rus_h_black_death.note: The Black Death reached Pskov and Novgorod in 1352 and Moscow in 1353, where Grand Prince Semyon the Proud, his sons and Metropolitan Theognostus died.
ev.rus_h_sergius.title: The Elder in the Forest
ev.rus_h_sergius.text: In the forests beyond Radonezh lives Abbot Sergius. He chops wood for cells and carries water himself, yet princes and peasants alike come to him. They say he can reconcile feuding princes with a single word.
ev.rus_h_sergius.note: Sergius of Radonezh (c. 1314–1392) founded the Trinity monastery around 1337–45. His disciples founded dozens of monasteries across northern Rus; he is one of the most revered Russian saints.
ev.rus_h_white_kremlin.title: The White-Stone Kremlin
ev.rus_h_white_kremlin.text: After the fire Prince Dmitry ordered the Kremlin rebuilt in stone. All winter white limestone is hauled over the ice from Myachkovo. Hands are needed, and they pay in silver.
ev.rus_h_white_kremlin.cart: Haul stone with your own horse
ev.rus_h_white_kremlin.note: The white-stone Kremlin was built in 1367–68 under Dmitry Ivanovich. In 1368 it already withstood a siege by Grand Duke Algirdas of Lithuania.
ev.rus_h_kulikovo.title: To the Don, Beyond the Nepryadva
ev.rus_h_kulikovo.text: The warlord Mamai is marching on Rus with the whole Horde. Grand Prince Dmitry is gathering his regiments at Kolomna, an army such as Rus has never seen. They say Abbot Sergius blessed him and gave him two warrior monks.
ev.rus_h_kulikovo.go.success: On Kulikovo Field the Horde fled. You came home alive and are greeted as a hero.
ev.rus_h_kulikovo.go.failure: You lay among the fallen until your own people found you.
ev.rus_h_kulikovo.note: On 8 September 1380 Dmitry Ivanovich's army defeated Mamai on Kulikovo Field where the Nepryadva joins the Don. Dmitry was later called Donskoy. Dependence on the Horde continued for another century.
ev.rus_h_tokhtamysh.title: Tokhtamysh at Moscow
ev.rus_h_tokhtamysh.text: Khan Tokhtamysh has reached Moscow; Prince Dmitry has gone to raise an army. For three days the townspeople fought from the walls. Now the khan's envoys swear he will harm no one if the gates are opened.
ev.rus_h_tokhtamysh.gates: Believe them and go out with the procession
ev.rus_h_tokhtamysh.gates.success: The massacre began right at the gates, but you managed to slip away in the crush.
ev.rus_h_tokhtamysh.gates.failure: It was a trick: the Horde burst into the city, cutting down everyone in their path.
ev.rus_h_tokhtamysh.flee: Climb down the wall at night and run
ev.rus_h_tokhtamysh.flee.success: You got away through the woods. Moscow burned, but you are alive.
ev.rus_h_tokhtamysh.flee.failure: You were caught by the river and driven off to the Horde.
ev.rus_h_tokhtamysh.note: On 26 August 1382 Tokhtamysh took Moscow by trickery and burned it, killing many inhabitants. Grand Prince Dmitry was again forced to pay tribute to the Horde.
ev.rus_h_dark_one.title: The Blinded Prince
ev.rus_h_dark_one.text: Dmitry Shemyaka seized Grand Prince Vasily at prayer in the Trinity monastery and had him blinded. Now Vasily is called the Dark, and Shemyaka sits in Moscow. But many boyars and servicemen are going over to the blind prince.
ev.rus_h_dark_one.note: The feudal war of 1425–53 between Vasily II and his uncle and cousins was the worst civil war of the Muscovite principality. In 1446 Vasily was blinded, but a year later he regained the throne.
ev.rus_h_shelon.title: The Shelon
ev.rus_h_shelon.text: Novgorod sought the Lithuanian king's protection, and Ivan III declared war. The Novgorod army, craftsmen forced onto horses, rides out against the Muscovite regiments to the river Shelon.
ev.rus_h_shelon.fight.success: The army was routed, but you escaped from the field.
ev.rus_h_shelon.fight.failure: The Muscovite cavalry crushed the militia. You were wounded and robbed.
ev.rus_h_shelon.avoid: Pay your way out of the campaign
ev.rus_h_shelon.note: On 14 July 1471 the Muscovite army crushed the Novgorodians on the river Shelon. By the Peace of Korostyn Novgorod renounced its alliance with Lithuania, the first step towards losing its independence.
ev.rus_h_novgorod_fall.title: The Bell Is Taken
ev.rus_h_novgorod_fall.text: Ivan III declared: "There shall be no veche bell in our patrimony, no posadnik; we shall hold the state ourselves." The veche bell has been taken down and is being carted to Moscow. The city kisses the cross to the Muscovite sovereign.
ev.rus_h_novgorod_fall.swear: Kiss the cross and get on with life
ev.rus_h_novgorod_fall.note: In January 1478 the Novgorod Republic was annexed by Moscow: the veche was abolished, the bell carried off, and mass deportations followed in the 1480s.
ev.rus_h_ugra.title: The Stand on the Ugra
ev.rus_h_ugra.text: Khan Akhmat reached the river Ugra, and Ivan III's army stood on the far bank. For weeks the two armies faced each other, exchanging fire across the water. Then frost set in, and the khan turned back. No more tribute goes to the Horde.
ev.rus_h_ugra.note: The Stand on the Ugra in autumn 1480 ended with the retreat of Khan Akhmat of the Great Horde. It is regarded as the end of Rus's dependence on the Horde.
ev.rus_h_tsar_1547.title: The Tsar
ev.rus_h_tsar_1547.text: Sixteen-year-old Grand Prince Ivan Vasilyevich has been crowned in the Dormition Cathedral with the Cap of Monomakh, crowned as tsar like the Byzantine emperors. The sovereign is now called Tsar of All Rus.
ev.rus_h_tsar_1547.note: On 16 January 1547 Ivan IV became the first Muscovite ruler to be formally crowned tsar.
ev.rus_h_fire_1547.title: The Great Fire
ev.rus_h_fire_1547.text: In summer almost all of Moscow burned: the Kremlin, Kitai-gorod, the suburbs. A rumour spreads that the Glinskys, the tsar's relatives, worked sorcery, sprinkling houses with water steeped in human hearts. A mob is marching to the tsar at Vorobyovo.
ev.rus_h_fire_1547.riot.success: The tsar spoke to the crowd and everyone dispersed. Though one of the Glinskys had already been killed.
ev.rus_h_fire_1547.riot.failure: Musketeers met the crowd with gunfire. You were hurt.
ev.rus_h_fire_1547.note: The fire of 21 June 1547 destroyed most of Moscow and killed about 1,700 people. It was followed by a rising against the Glinskys, after which the young Ivan IV began his reforms.
ev.rus_h_kazan.title: The Taking of Kazan
ev.rus_h_kazan.text: The tsar is leading a huge army against Kazan. Tunnels packed with gunpowder are dug under the walls, and mobile wooden forts and cannon towers are raised. Men are needed.
ev.rus_h_kazan.go.success: The mines exploded, the walls collapsed and Kazan fell. You came home with plunder.
ev.rus_h_kazan.go.failure: You were wounded in the assault.
ev.rus_h_kazan.note: On 2 October 1552 Ivan IV's army stormed Kazan after blowing up its walls. To celebrate, the Cathedral of the Intercession (St Basil's) was built on Red Square. Astrakhan fell in 1556.
ev.rus_h_livonian.title: The Livonian War
ev.rus_h_livonian.text: The tsar is fighting for access to the Baltic Sea: first Livonia, then Lithuania, Poland and Sweden. The war drags on for years, taxes rise, and every plough-unit must supply soldiers and carts.
ev.rus_h_livonian.serve.success: You came back from Polotsk alive and with your pay.
ev.rus_h_livonian.serve.failure: You were wounded in Livonia and took a long time to recover.
ev.rus_h_livonian.note: The Livonian War (1558–1583) began well but ended with the loss of all gains and a ruined country. The north-western lands, especially Novgorod's, were depopulated.
ev.rus_h_oprichnina.title: The Oprichnina
ev.rus_h_oprichnina.text: The tsar has split the country into the oprichnina and the zemshchina. Riders in black gallop through the streets with dogs' heads and brooms at their saddles, "to bite traitors and sweep away treason". People are taken at night, and no one knows why.
ev.rus_h_oprichnina.silent: Keep quiet and keep your head down
ev.rus_h_oprichnina.note: The oprichnina (1565–1572) was Ivan IV's reign of terror: executions of boyars and commoners and the ruin of lands seized for the "sovereign's domain". It shattered the country's economy.
ev.rus_h_novgorod_1570.title: The Tsar's Pogrom
ev.rus_h_novgorod_1570.text: The tsar has come to Novgorod with his oprichniki on a denunciation of treason. For six weeks they loot monasteries, shops and homes, and drown people in the Volkhov. The city is frozen with terror.
ev.rus_h_novgorod_1570.hide.success: The oprichniki passed your yard by, taking only the livestock and grain.
ev.rus_h_novgorod_1570.hide.failure: They found you and dragged you into the street.
ev.rus_h_novgorod_1570.note: The sack of Novgorod in January–February 1570 was Ivan IV's punitive expedition, in which thousands of townspeople died. The exact number of victims is unknown and estimates vary widely.
ev.rus_h_moscow_1571.title: Devlet Giray Burns Moscow
ev.rus_h_moscow_1571.text: The Crimean khan Devlet Giray slipped past the defences on the Oka and reached Moscow. The Tatars set fire to the suburbs and the wind drove the flames into the city; in three hours everything but the Kremlin burned. People are crushed in the gateways and drowning in the river.
ev.rus_h_moscow_1571.stone.success: The stone walls withstood the heat. You walked out into the ashes alive.
ev.rus_h_moscow_1571.stone.failure: People choked on the smoke inside the church.
ev.rus_h_moscow_1571.river.success: You stood in the water up to your neck until the fire burned out.
ev.rus_h_moscow_1571.river.failure: In the crush on the bank you were knocked off your feet.
ev.rus_h_moscow_1571.flee: Run across the fields away from the city
ev.rus_h_moscow_1571.flee.success: You got away, and behind you a black column of smoke stood over Moscow.
ev.rus_h_moscow_1571.flee.failure: In the fields the Tatars caught you and drove you off to Crimea.
ev.rus_h_moscow_1571.note: On 24 May 1571 the Crimean khan Devlet I Giray burned Moscow. Tens of thousands died and even more were driven into captivity. A year later, in 1572, his army was defeated at Molodi.
ev.rus_h_famine_1570.title: Famine and Plague
ev.rus_h_famine_1570.text: For three years rain has ruined the grain. The price of rye has risen tenfold, beggars wander the roads, and plague has followed the famine. Villages stand empty.
ev.rus_h_famine_1570.note: The famine of 1569–71, together with plague, the oprichnina and the Livonian War, left the central and north-western lands of Muscovy deserted.
ev.rus_h_molodi.title: Molodi
ev.rus_h_molodi.text: The Crimean khan was marching on Moscow again, and at the village of Molodi the commander Mikhail Vorotynsky stopped him. The mobile fort, the musketeers and the cavalry held for five days. The horde fled.
ev.rus_h_molodi.note: The Battle of Molodi (July–August 1572) was a major victory over Devlet Giray's Crimean and Ottoman army, ending his attempts to subjugate Moscow.
ev.rus_h_reserved_years.title: The Forbidden Years
ev.rus_h_reserved_years.text: It has been announced: there will be no St George's Day this year; peasants are forbidden to leave. Whoever leaves his landlord will be hunted down and returned. The old men shake their heads: "So much for St George's Day."
ev.rus_h_reserved_years.stay: Stay: where else would you go?
ev.rus_h_reserved_years.run.success: You went off to the southern lands, where the servicemen need ploughmen and nobody asks for papers.
ev.rus_h_reserved_years.run.failure: You were tracked down, brought back and punished besides.
ev.rus_h_reserved_years.note: From 1581 Muscovy introduced "forbidden years" in which peasants could not move on St George's Day. In 1597 a five-year limit was set for hunting runaways. This is how serfdom took shape.
ev.rus_h_great_famine.title: The Great Famine
ev.rus_h_great_famine.text: It rained all summer, and in August a frost struck: the grain died in the fields. The second and third years were the same. People eat grass and hay and die on the roads. Tsar Boris is handing out bread and money in Moscow, and crowds are streaming there.
ev.rus_h_great_famine.tsar_bread: Go to the capital for the tsar's alms
ev.rus_h_great_famine.share: Open your granaries to the hungry
ev.rus_h_great_famine.note: The famine of 1601–03, probably caused by cooling after the eruption of the Huaynaputina volcano in Peru, killed by some estimates up to a third of Muscovy's population and opened the Time of Troubles.
